historical_prior.note: Baseline empirical-Bayes prior only; intended to be replaced/refined as the model develops.

notes: ESPN projected season points are converted to PPG using 17 NFL games.
ADP/rank are retained as market variables and are not folded into the production posterior.
Historical weekly SD is treated as predictive/aleatoric variance.
Historical latent-mean uncertainty includes an empirical year-to-year transition term estimated from nflverse.
Projection uncertainty is inferred from current ESPN-vs-history residual width after subtracting historical transition uncertainty in quadrature.
Replacement counts are a preseason prior and will become dynamic as actual rosters are drafted.
FLEX starter allocation is computed globally after mandatory starter slots are filled.
Draft value is position-relative; raw PPG is retained only as the production observable.
ADP/rank remain market observables and are not included in VORP.
Players on nfl_team=FA are excluded from the current draftable universe.
History-only players require a credible current ESPN market rank; stale historical names cannot define replacement levels.
ESPN ADP is the market-selection center when it is below the apparent ~170 undrafted/sentinel region.
ESPN rank is used as a fallback market center and as an empirical dispersion diagnostic.
Pick-survival probabilities are conditioned on the player already being available at the current pick.
ESPN ID is the canonical live-draft player key.
Drafted players are removed from the available universe before recommendations.
Remaining replacement demand is updated from actual drafted position counts.
Opponent simulations use conditional market pick hazards, then modestly adjust for team roster need.
Candidate utility includes immediate dynamic VORP plus option value from what is expected to survive to the next user pick.
Fast SHORT TURN uses an analytical sequential contingency engine rather than generic Monte Carlo.
Fast LONG TURN samples conditional market draft times in vectorized NumPy arrays and freezes dynamic values over the one-turn horizon.
Deep mode retains the slower team-need-aware sequential Monte Carlo for cross-checking.
Current-pick and forecast values are marginal utility to the user roster, not league-wide positional VORP alone.
Starter utility is the best legal QB/RB/RB/WR/WR/TE/FLEX assignment measured above dynamic positional replacement.
Players who do not improve the starting lineup retain discounted bench/option value rather than zero value.
Bench value decays with same-position depth so repeated RB/WR accumulation has diminishing marginal utility.
Candidate generation reserves a small cross-position floor before filling remaining slots by roster marginal utility.
By default K/DST are not legal recommendations until the 14 QB/RB/WR/TE roster capacity is filled.
Core capacity is derived from active roster size minus required specialist slots; IR is excluded.
Current-pick candidate ranking is expected final 16-player roster utility, not one-turn marginal value.
FAST uses sampled conditional market orders through the end of round 16.
DEEP uses the same final-roster objective but applies opponent team needs within a market-order queue.
Bench coverage weights are derived from how many starting/FLEX slots a position can cover, then decay with same-position depth.
Short-turn contingency remains an explanation layer in FAST but no longer drives the ranking objective.
FAST defaults to 40 common-random-number full drafts for draft-clock latency; DEEP defaults to 30 team-aware full drafts.
Bench depth decay is applied globally across the shared BENCH pool, not reset independently for each position.
Two complete 192-pick Aug 30 mocks are stored for empirical calibration diagnostics.
Behavior weighting remains disabled until at least three complete mocks are available.
Future mocks can be imported with the import-mock command.
Every DEEP run persists a reusable bank of latent market-order scenarios.
Observed opponent picks reweight the bank with the same team-need-aware opponent choice model used by DEEP.
FAST resamples primarily from the conditioned DEEP posterior and mixes a small fresh market component for robustness.
Subsequent DEEP refreshes reuse healthy posterior particles and add fresh scenarios rather than forgetting previous observed-draft information.
ESS = 1/sum(w^2) measures how much of the bank remains supported by actual draft behavior; low ESS increases fresh-scenario mixing.
Final roster utility is evaluated week by week rather than through a generic bench-depth credit.
Known NFL byes are deterministic unavailability; other missed-game events are modeled as common-random-number availability shocks.
A bench player earns value only when he actually enters the best legal weekly lineup above replacement.
Bye overlap has no arbitrary penalty. It matters only through weekly lineup feasibility and expected scoring.
The current availability probabilities are conservative model knobs, not claimed player-specific injury forecasts; they can later be calibrated from historical games missed.
Playoff weeks use league-average participation priors until season-specific playoff probability is modeled.
The terminal objective is expected weekly H2H win probability versus a generic league-strength lineup, not linear bye-loss PPG.
This nonlinearity allows either clustered or spread bye weeks to win when the simulated H2H consequences justify it.
v0.27 retains the v0.26 OUT/ACTIVE_LIMITED/ACTIVE_FULL state decomposition and lock-aware information policy.
Current-week status supplies the prior for P(active) and P(full|active); NFL.com practice (preferred) or Sleeper practice updates those priors in Bayesian odds space.
Only the latest practice state plus one trajectory summary are used so correlated daily practice reports are not multiplied as independent observations.
The practice likelihood ratios are explicit UNCALIBRATED priors, preserved with provenance for later empirical reliability/Brier/workload calibration.
Hard-unavailable states and bye weeks remain P(active)=0 regardless of practice evidence.
FULL versus LIMITED workload remains latent to the realistic pregame policy unless explicitly forced in the lineup laboratory.
v0.27 uses 16384 predictive MC universes by default; 1024/4096/16384/65536 remain selectable in the GUI.
v0.27 evidence-conditions current-week P(active) and P(full|active) while preserving the v0.26 lock-aware policy and common-random-number semantics.

Current-week policy comparisons expose fixed, realistic lock-aware, idealized-active (all active/inactive known pre-lock, workload latent), and idealized-full (OUT/FULL/LIMITED known pre-lock) win probabilities; the report separates status-timing and workload-information advantages sequentially.
Lineups are selected from pregame operational means within each resolved availability branch; realized fantasy draws are used only to score the already-selected lineup, preventing look-ahead bias.
Common random numbers are keyed by player so HOLD and each action share availability, epistemic, game, and opponent universes.
Final action ranking reports mean paired delta, a paired-resample 68% interval for the mean effect, and strict P(+/0/- | acquired).
FREEAGENT acquisition probability is 1; WAIVERS acquisition probability remains a separate provisional opponent-behavior layer.
ESPN projections are explicit yield anchors and their model residuals are retained for later data/MC closure calibration.
v0.23 uses the nflverse matchup/kinematic acceptance layer.

v0.30 replaces the higher-priority-manager weakest-position waiver heuristic with a fast modeled best-add/drop roster-improvement signal; acquisition probability remains a separate uncalibrated behavior layer.
v0.30-fixed2 uses hierarchical paired action MC (1024 -> 4096 -> final configured N) and only escalates the small surviving frontier to full N.
v0.30-fixed2 adds explicit bench future-role option and replacement-scarcity utility for non-starting QB/RB/WR/TE players; no named-player protection rules are used.
v0.30-fixed3 replaces additive per-player bench premiums with roster-level portfolio upside and one-starter-out replacement-stress scarcity; auxiliary option value is projection-provenance aware.
v0.30-fixed3 requires raw paired predictive-MC support for ACTIONABLE_EDGE; auxiliary-only improvements are labeled ROSTER_OPTION_EDGE and do not trigger an immediate-action recommendation.

v0.30-fixed4 replaces deterministic bench stress tests with a small paired future-roster-state ensemble (common random numbers across HOLD/actions); scarcity is diagnostic-only by default to avoid double counting.
v0.30-fixed4 adds classification-aware MC futility stopping using a conservative Wilson upper bound on P(better), and exposes whole-league opponent-reference construction in progress output.

v0.30-fixed6 makes predictive-MC futility raw-only: contingent roster-option probability is reportable at its current SCREEN stage but can never trigger larger 4096/16384 football-MC stages; the broad screen also protects contingent losses without letting positive speculative option value dominate predictive ranking.

v0.30-fixed6 reframes add/drop valuation as a paired counterfactual league-state response: a released player is propagated through the waiver transition kernel into likely recipient rosters and those roster changes are evaluated with the same commissioned predictive football model at small N.

v0.30-fixed6 removes the fixed4/fixed5 contingent option/scarcity term from authoritative action utility; that ensemble remains screening/diagnostic-only. Predictive-MC escalation follows the league-state paired response.
v0.31 restricts the ordinary player market to QB/RB/WR/TE; D/ST and K are evaluated in dedicated same-channel management layers.

v0.35-fixed1 keeps the deterministic future player-lineup calculation as candidate screening only; a future self-player FREEAGENT swap changes P_w only after paired predictive H2H CRN confirmation reuses the commissioned player MC and existing ACTIONABLE/POSSIBLE thresholds.
v0.23 treats ESPN projections as an explicit external predicted-yield anchor rather than ground truth.
A current-week ESPN anchor is treated as already evaluated at ESPN's implicit acceptance point; our K applies to the internal model branch before the weak ensemble.
ESPN season/17 is a weaker neutral anchor and receives the weekly K adjustment with the neutral model ensemble.
latent_mean_sd_ppg is epistemic model uncertainty; matchup/kinematic uncertainty and residual game-to-game variance are retained separately.
v0.23 treats matchup as a week-dependent acceptance/kinematic layer, not a permanent player-talent adjustment.
Opponent defense observables come from nflverse play-by-play and are standardized only after current-season measurements are shrunk toward the prior season with lambda=N_current/(N_current+k).
Current-week ESPN projections are treated as external predictions already evaluated at an implicit acceptance point, so our K correction is applied to the internal model branch before ESPN anchoring.
DST is simulated from sacks, turnovers, defensive touchdowns, points allowed, and yards allowed, then passed through the exact ESPN nonlinear bucket scoring response.
v0.28 treats the learned player x defense interaction as a higher-order Data/MC correction to the commissioned base predictive yield.
The correction grids are fitted offline from underlying football statistics only; fantasy points are never a fit target.
Weekly MC evaluates precomputed grids by interpolation and propagates finite-grid uncertainty through a separate deterministic random stream.
Each component grid is chronologically held out on the latest configured training season; grids that fail to improve closure are neutralized operationally and remain diagnostic-only.
The existing v0.23 K layer remains part of the base MC and the v0.28 correction is applied on top as a separately auditable higher-order response.
v0.28-fixed4: when commissioned_only=true, SHADOW grids are diagnostic-only and contribute neither operational mean shift nor operational interaction variance.
v0.29 freezes immutable pregame component/yield states and joins them to postgame nflverse weekly observations.
Fantasy-yield closure uses availability-marginalized pregame moments; opportunity counts are workload-marginalized while efficiency rates remain conditional football quantities.
Missing nflverse stat rows are not interpreted as inactive. Availability Brier scoring requires explicit active/inactive truth.
closure-update refreshes current-season weekly stats by default; use --cached only for an intentional offline rebuild.
Closure diagnostics never refit the predictive model automatically.
v0.30 evaluates trade roster value with the same detailed predictive player model used by weekly/waiver decisions; partner response is a separate uncalibrated behavior layer.
No external generic trade-value chart is used. The independent market-perception channel uses ESPN projected production plus public ownership/trend observables.
Trade-search screening is only candidate generation; selected offers are reevaluated with paired predictive MC.
Unequal 1-for-2 or 2-for-1 packages may require one modeled best legal post-trade release, which is always surfaced explicitly.
Acceptance, counteroffer, and rejection probabilities are provisional until actual league trade behavior provides calibration data.
v0.31 trade evaluation/search is player-channel only (QB/RB/WR/TE); K/DST are not trade-market assets in this model.
Positive carry synergy is retained as a schedule-complementarity diagnostic; fixed2 does not treat the best-static-DST baseline as a commissioned streaming policy.
D/ST candidates are compared only with D/ST configurations.
Two-defense value is pregame weekly rotation synergy; realized MC is never used to choose the weekly starter.
If a second D/ST requires a roster slot, the slot cost is requested separately from the QB/RB/WR/TE player channel.
Team aliases such as WAS->WSH are normalized before schedule/implied-points lookup.
K candidates are compared only with K configurations.
Weekly matchup response uses the existing schedule game total/team implied-points coordinate as an uncalibrated prior pending prospective kicker closure.
A second kicker is disabled by default.
v0.32 adds a dynamic same-channel specialist league-state policy and paired complete-state carry2 confirmation without modifying player-channel production physics.
v0.31-fixed2 normalizes specialist NFL team aliases through the shared nflverse normalization map before bye/schedule lookup.
v0.31-fixed2 labels same-channel season comparisons as static swaps; it does not claim a dynamic future streaming market policy.
v0.31-fixed2 demotes positive two-DST carry results to diagnostic screens until a one-slot streaming policy and paired complete-state confirmation are commissioned.
v0.31 introduces channel separation: player market P={QB,RB,WR,TE}, defense D={DST}, kicker K={K}.
Channels are compared internally; they are combined only when evaluating a complete roster state.
Player-market and trade candidate generation exclude K/DST. Specialist management uses dedicated weekly matchup/synergy response functions.
No new action-value tuning coefficient is introduced; a manager swaps only when the pregame expected same-channel response strictly improves.
Current FREEAGENT specialists are guaranteed initial market states. Current WAIVERS are excluded from the guaranteed pool rather than assigned a fabricated acquisition probability.
A dropped specialist re-enters the modeled market in the following week, preventing a same-week recursive claim artifact.
Future simultaneous specialist demand is ordered by current ESPN waiver priority as an explicit uncalibrated proxy until observed specialist transaction behavior can calibrate a richer kernel.
Realized Monte Carlo outcomes never select a transaction or starter.
